parsed.explanation: Structural and documented signals point to severe risk. Article 135 criminalises same-sex conduct with custodial penalties, and reported enforcement includes torture during investigation, humiliating interrogation, and confinement to mental hospitals. A 2019 case documents prolonged state torture of a gay doctor, and a 2020 case documents arrests of modelling figures. The dossier says a trans visitor's exposure turns on how authorities read birth-sex status, so trans women with male documents fall within the statute's scope. There is no anti-discrimination law, no recourse, and official justification framed around threats to society. Trans-specific incident data is absent and media is state-controlled, so the rating rests on structural extrapolation and enforcement-linked harms rather than measured frequency. Legal-recognition absence is resident-facing and weighted lightly. Sexuality law is treated as a trans lever because enforcement against gender-nonconforming and same-sex-attracted people is documented.
